synthetic image of the object in a canonical pose. We show that the 6D pose of
the object in the input image can be estimated by finding the pose that
minimizes the difference between the input image and the synthetic image

which is based on the spatial modulation (SM) technique. In the proposed scheme,
the base station (BS) uses the SM technique to transmit the pilot signal to
different users, and the users can be distinguished by the different
transmitting antennas. The proposed scheme can effectively reduce the pilot
contamination problem and improve the system performance. Simulation results
show that the proposed scheme can achieve a significant performance gain
compared to the traditional pilot reuse scheme.

nonlinear incidence rate and time-varying parameters. We propose a
least-squares-based approach to estimate the parameters of the model. We
establish the consistency of the estimator and provide a central limit theorem
for the estimator. We also propose a bootstrap-based approach to construct
confidence intervals for the parameters. We illustrate the performance of the
proposed methods using simulated data and real data from the COVID-19 pandemic.

a Bayesian approach.
  From a methodological perspective, the main contribution of this paper is the
derivation of the asymptotic distribution of the least-squares estimator for a
nonlinear SIR model with time-varying parameters. The main challenge in
deriving the asymptotic distribution is the fact that the model is nonlinear and
the parameters are time-varying. To overcome this challenge, we use a
generalization of the approach proposed by Janssen and Nijman (1991) for
estimating the parameters of a nonlinear regression model with time-varying
parameters. The main practical contribution of this paper is the application of
the proposed methods to real data from the COVID-19 pandemic.

bootstrap-based approach to construct confidence intervals for the parameters.

simulated data and real data from the COVID-19 pandemic. In Section 7, we

remarks.

(PNe) are the final stages of evolution of
low- to intermediate-mass stars. They are the most common type of extragalactic
ionized nebulae and are used as probes of the interstellar medium (ISM) in
galaxies. PNe are also used as distance indicators, and their kinematics can
provide insights into the dynamics of galaxies. In this paper, we present a
catalog of PNe in the nearby galaxy M101, which is the largest catalog of PNe
in this galaxy to date. We present the results of our observations, which were
obtained using the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and the Keck Observatory. We
present the catalog of PNe in M101, which includes 1,444 PNe, and we present
their properties, including their positions, sizes, and fluxes. We also
present the kinematics of the PNe in M101, which we obtained using the
HST/STIS and HST/WFC3 instruments. We present the radial velocities of the PNe
in M101, which range from -150 to 250 km/s, and we present their velocity
dispersions, which range from 10 to 50 km/s. We also present the rotation
curves of the PNe in M101, which we obtained by fitting the velocity
dispersions of the PNe as a function of their distances from the center of the
galaxy. We present the rotation curve of M101, which we obtained by combining
the rotation curves of the PNe with the rotation curve of the stars in the
galaxy. We also present the mass models of M101, which we obtained by
combining the rotation curve of the PNe with the rotation curve of the stars in
the galaxy. We present the total mass of M101, which is 1.1 x 10^12 M_sun, and
we present the mass-to-light ratio of the galaxy, which is 1.4 M_sun/L_sun.
Finally, we present the implications of our results for the study of the
dynamics of galaxies.

machine learning model. In this paper, we propose a novel loss function called
the "Sigmoid-Logistic Loss" (SLL) for binary classification problems. The SLL
function is a combination of the sigmoid and logistic loss functions. We
theoretically prove that the SLL function converges to the logistic loss
function as the sigmoid function approaches the step function. We also
theoretically prove that the SLL function is a convex function. We empirically
evaluate the performance of the SLL function on several binary classification
datasets. Our results show that the SLL function outperforms the logistic loss
function on several datasets.

generalize IL policies to unseen situations by leveraging the structure of
human demonstrations. We introduce a novel framework called Hierarchical
Imitation Learning (HIL) that learns a hierarchical policy structure from
demonstrations. The policy structure is learned by clustering the demonstrations
into a set of skills and then learning a policy for each skill. We propose a
novel hierarchical imitation learning algorithm that learns the policy structure
and the policies for each skill from demonstrations. We evaluate our approach on
two challenging robotic manipulation tasks and show that it outperforms
state-of-the-art IL baselines in terms of generalization to unseen situations.
We also show that our approach can be used to learn a hierarchical policy
structure from demonstrations that can be used to improve the generalization of
IL policies.

post-bounce waiting time before the onset of a supernova explosion can be
significantly longer than the dynamical timescale. In this paper, we present
the first 3D simulations of core collapse that include the long waiting time
before the explosion. We find that the long waiting time is crucial for the
formation of the standing accretion shock instability (SASI) and the
subsequent explosion. In particular, the long waiting time allows for the
formation of a large-scale, non-axisymmetric instability in the proto-neutron
star (PNS) that drives the explosion. We also find that the explosion is
sensitive to the initial conditions of the simulation, and that the explosion
mechanism is not yet fully understood. We discuss the implications of our

  \section{Introduction}
  Differentiable rendering has received increasing interest for its ability to
learn 3D representations from 2D images. However, existing methods are
inflexible and lack interpretability. In this work, we propose a novel
differentiable rendering framework that is capable of learning 3D
representations from 2D images in a flexible and interpretable manner. Our
framework is based on a novel differentiable rendering algorithm that can
render 3D scenes with complex occlusions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of
our framework on several 3D reconstruction tasks and show that it can learn
interpretable 3D representations from 2D images.
  \section{Related Work}
  \subsection{Differentiable Rendering}
  Differentiable rendering is a technique that allows us to compute the
derivative of a rendered image with respect to the 3D scene. This technique has
been used in several applications such as 3D reconstruction, image
synthesis, and image editing. However, existing methods are limited to simple
scenes with no occlusions. In this work, we propose a novel differentiable
rendering algorithm that can render 3D scenes with complex occlusions.
  \subsection{3D Reconstruction}
  3D reconstruction is a technique that allows us to recover the 3D structure
of a scene from 2D images. This technique has been used in several applications
such as robotics, autonomous driving, and surveillance. However, existing
methods are limited to simple scenes with no occlusions. In this work, we propose
a novel 3D reconstruction framework that can learn 3D representations from 2D
images in a flexible and interpretable manner.

combines causal graph theory with deep learning. CDL has been shown to be
effective in a variety of applications, including causal discovery, causal
inference, and causal policy learning. However, CDL is still in its infancy,
and there is a lack of theoretical understanding of its properties. In this
paper, we provide a theoretical analysis of CDL. We show that CDL is
equivalent to a class of causal generative models, and we provide a theoretical
guarantee for the identifiability of causal effects in CDL. We also provide a
new algorithm for causal policy learning based on CDL, and we show that it
achieves a lower regret bound than existing algorithms.

also provide a new perspective on the connections between CDL and causal
generative models.

  \section{Introduction}
  End-to-end (E2E) neural automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems have
achieved remarkable performance in recent years. However, they are still
sensitive to noise and reverberation. In this paper, we propose a novel approach
to improve the robustness of E2E ASR systems by incorporating a generative
adversarial network (GAN) into the training process. The GAN is used to generate
clean speech from noisy speech, and the generated clean speech is used as an
auxiliary input to the E2E ASR system. We evaluate the proposed approach on the
AISHell-1 and AISHELL-2 datasets and show that it achieves significant
improvements in robustness to noise and reverberation.
  \section{Related Work}

reverberation. To improve the robustness of E2E ASR systems, various approaches

proposed in \cite{zhang2020improving,liu2020improving}. In addition, E2E ASR
systems have been proposed to be robust to reverberation in

higher levels of poverty, lower levels of education, and lower levels of
income are more likely to have unmet health care needs. We also find that
individuals living in areas with higher levels of poverty, lower levels of
education, and lower levels of income are less likely to have health insurance.

associated with health care utilization in the United States. Policymakers should
consider the impact of social determinants on health care utilization when
designing policies to improve health care access and outcomes.

  \section{Introduction}
  Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) has achieved remarkable success in solving
complex tasks, such as playing Atari games and robotic control. However, the
performance of DRL algorithms is often limited by the lack of exploration in the
state space. In particular, the DQN algorithm~\cite{mnih2015human} uses an
$\epsilon$-greedy strategy to explore the state space, which is not effective
for complex tasks. In this paper, we propose a novel curiosity-driven DRL
algorithm, called Curiosity-Driven Deep Q-Network (CD-DQN), which uses a novel
curiosity-driven exploration strategy to learn complex tasks.
  The proposed algorithm uses a novelty prediction network to predict the
novelty of the current state. The novelty prediction network is trained to
predict the novelty of the current state using the past experiences. The
novelty prediction is then used to compute the exploration bonus, which is used
to update the Q-network. We evaluate the performance of CD-DQN on two complex
tasks, namely, the Atari game Montezuma's Revenge and the robotic task of
learning to navigate a maze. The results show that CD-DQN outperforms state-of-
the-art algorithms on both tasks.

operation. The CEPC will be able to study the Higgs boson decay into two

) frequencies is a promising technology for
high-speed wireless communication systems. However, the THz channel is
characterized by a high path loss and a low coherence time, which makes the
channel estimation a challenging task. In this paper, we propose a novel
channel estimation method for THz communication systems. The proposed method
exploits the spatial diversity of the THz channel to estimate the channel
impulse response (CIR) at the base station (BS) side. The proposed method
consists of two stages: the first stage is a pilot-based channel estimation
stage, where the BS transmits a pilot signal to the user equipment (UE) and the
UE estimates the CIR. The second stage is a spatial channel estimation stage,
where the BS estimates the CIR using the estimated CIR at the UE. The proposed
method is evaluated using numerical simulations and the results show that the
proposed method outperforms the conventional pilot-based channel estimation
method.

Finally, we present numerical results for the evaluation of the post-Newtonian
metric in the merger of two compact objects, and we show that the new method is
more efficient than the standard method.
